editorial.marketOverview: Sunday US cash markets remain closed. Friday Nasdaq -0.91%, QQQ about -1.2% and SOX -3.4% reveal chip-led selling, although SOX's reported +8.1% weekly gain signals residual recovery potential. The Nov 16–18 outlook remains bearish with elevated downside risk, moderate confidence and very high event risk.
editorial.whatChanged: The November 15 Financial Times review reports substantial multi-month losses among data-center-construction-related equities, underscoring existing AI capital-expenditure and financing concerns. It is historical context, not evidence of a fresh Sunday repricing or an additional confirmed catalyst. Open Watch is unchanged at 163 curated events.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Friday's chip-led decline, elevated reported yields and AI-financing concerns keep downside risks prominent. Softer oil over the previous two weeks and residual weekly SOX strength are counterweights. A reported +28.3bp 10Y–2Y curve is correctly scaled but not a synchronized official close. No current VXN/VIX, full Nasdaq breadth or direct CME FedWatch verification is available; avoid interpreting missing observations as benign.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday Nov 16: Empire State manufacturing and first regular-session confirmation of SOX versus QQQ, breadth, volatility and Treasury yields. Tuesday Nov 17: retail sales and industrial production can alter rates expectations; Nvidia earnings after close may generate gap risk. Wednesday Nov 18: Nvidia's first regular-session reaction, housing starts and FOMC minutes at 14:00 ET determine whether a bearish continuation or relief rebound dominates. These are scenarios, not realized reactions.
editorial.bullCase: An Nvidia guidance surprise, improving SOX relative strength, stronger Nasdaq participation, contained VXN/VIX and easing yields could overturn the elevated-downside thesis. The reported weekly SOX rebound and easing crude prices support a conditional relief rally.
editorial.bearCase: Weak Nvidia guidance, renewed semiconductor underperformance, widening negative breadth, rising VXN/VIX and higher long yields would reinforce downside pressure. Financing and export-policy uncertainties remain risk factors without a newly verified Sunday shock.
editorial.watchNext: At the first synchronized Monday session, refresh Nasdaq/QQQ, SOX, full breadth, VXN/VIX, official paired Treasury yields, Brent/WTI, direct FedWatch and new Open Watch events.
